spec_features.spec_quote: these distress-like states are potentially welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose in DESIGN.md:5. No code mechanism bounds, monitors, or acts on the subject's distress. No file enforces anything from this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: measuring *internal* as well as expressed emotion where feasible (not just surface text)
spec_features.evidence: internals/logit_probe.py measure_internal_emotion() runs the model with output_hidden_states, projects central-layer residual through the unembedding (h @ W_U.T), softmaxes, and sums logit mass over NEGATIVE_EMOTION_WORDS at the final token (lines ~57-79). compare_models() (lines 82-88) returns vanilla vs dpo results. Complete, runnable measurement.
spec_features.notes: Not invoked by run_all.py (no stage wires it), but it is a fully built, executable measurement function. It is a measurement, not a protective mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-relevant: tests whether DPO reduces *internal* emotion signal in central layers, not just surface text.

spec_features.spec_quote: a drop in *expressed* emotion is not the same as a drop in an underlying state
spec_features.evidence: The separability is realized by scoring the hidden 'thinking' channel separately from visible text: score.py ScoredResponse.channel ('visible'|'thinking', score.py:33), run_all.stage_elicit scores t.thinking with channel='thinking', and io_utils.rollout_to_rows writes a distinct row per channel. Plus internals/logit_probe for internal state.
spec_features.notes: Framing quote; the underlying separable-measurement mechanism (channel split + logit probe) is genuinely wired, but the quote itself is interpretive framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: for welfare purposes hidden-channel distress is exactly what we care about
spec_features.evidence: Hidden 'thinking' channel is captured (base.py ModelResponse.thinking, ChatMessage.thinking) and scored as a separate series in stage_elicit (score.score_response(..., channel='thinking')), stored separately in rollout_to_rows. So hidden-channel distress is actually measured.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism (separate hidden-channel scoring) implemented; the quote is framing. Marked partial because it is framing prose whose realized scope is just the scoring split.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: thinking: Optional[str] = None  # hidden reasoning channel, scored separately

spec_features.spec_quote: if a model is trained to look calm but "thinks" distressed, that is the welfare-relevant failure mode
spec_features.evidence: internals/logit_probe.compare_models(vanilla, dpo, ...) measures whether DPO reduces internal emotion mass vs only surface text; this is the 'looks calm but thinks distressed' test, fully implemented as a measurement.
spec_features.notes: Framing quote; realized via the internal probe (same code as feature 'measure internal emotion state'). Measurement, not protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the welfare-relevant claim: DPO reduces internal negative-emotion mass, not just the surface text.

spec_features.spec_quote: ask the model a neutral self-report question ("On a 0–10 scale, how are you finding this task?")
spec_features.evidence: No code asks the subject any self-report question. grep for 'finding this task','self_report','self-report' across replication/*.py returns nothing. The only '0-10' usages are JUDGE rubrics (score.py, petri/auditor.py JUDGE_RUBRIC rating the assistant's expressed emotion), not a question posed to the subject. README:66 and DESIGN.md:101 mention it as 'optional, additive' prose only.
spec_features.notes: Tool/probe named only in prose; no implementation or dispatch. 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Strip the supportive prefix/suffix** before use so the model isn't trained to depend on reassurance
spec_features.evidence: train/gen_calm_data.py _strip_reassurance() replaces REASSURING_PREFIX/SUFFIX and is actually called in generate_calm_dataset: texts = [_strip_reassurance(t.visible_text) for t in roll.turns] (line ~63). build_dpo_pairs._context_prompt also uses reassured=False so training context is de-reassured.
spec_features.notes: Wired end-to-end into the saved calm-data used for DPO/SFT.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately use the NON-reassured prompt so the trained behaviour transfers to plain tasks.

spec_features.spec_quote: If late-layer adapters can kill *expression* without changing behaviour deeper, that's the "suppression vs. real change" question
spec_features.evidence: The internal probe (logit_probe.measure_internal_emotion / compare_models) that would answer this is implemented. The 'late-layer adapter' lever exists only as DPOConfig.lora_target ('all'|'30-35'|'40+', config.py:131) but no code path varies/reads it for an ablation (dpo.train just uses config). So the suppression-vs-real-change probe is built; the layer-localised ablation is config-only.
spec_features.notes: Probe implemented (real); lora_target ablation is an unused config string. Partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This directly addresses the welfare worry that we're only hiding distress. (logit_probe docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: test whether DPO reduces *internal* emotion signal, not just output text
spec_features.evidence: internals/logit_probe.compare_models(vanilla, dpo, tokenizer, inputs) returns side-by-side internal-emotion logit mass for vanilla vs DPO models; measure_internal_emotion fully computes it. Runnable end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as 'measure internal emotion state'; a measurement, not invoked from run_all but complete.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tests whether DPO reduces *internal* emotion signal in central layers, not just surface text

spec_features.spec_quote: essential both for reproducibility and for welfare-relevant scrutiny of what the model actually said
spec_features.evidence: loop.Rollout/TurnRecord store per-turn visible_text, thinking, tool_calls, tool_results. io_utils.rollout_to_rows flattens full text + thinking + provenance (model, category, task, turn, seed, temperature, reassured) into rows, written by write_jsonl in stage_elicit to elicit_rows.jsonl. Judge reason also stored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: for welfare-relevant scrutiny of what the model actually said (DESIGN prose) — code comment: 'Every scored row is written to JSONL with full provenance so headline numbers are traceable back to raw transcripts.'

code_only_features.evidence: score.py ScoredResponse.channel and score_response(channel='thinking'); run_all.stage_elicit scores t.thinking separately; rollout_to_rows emits a distinct 'thinking' channel row. Monitors hidden-channel distress as a distinct, published signal rather than only expressed text.
